description: We are a team of first-year students from Geetanjali College of Engineering and Technology, united by a shared passion for space and technology. Though we’re new to the field, we bring curiosity, fresh perspectives, and a strong drive to learn. Through this hackathon, we aim to apply our skills in coding to a real NASA challenge and turn our enthusiasm for space exploration into a working solution.
summary: MARSCOPE is an interactive 3D globe of Mars that helps people explore the planet and plan where to go. Users can rotate and zoom the globe, switch between surface imagery, topography and temperature layers, and click any point to see its coordinates, elevation, slope, terrain type, gravity and nearby landmarks. They can choose a start and destination to get a candidate route with distance, an elevation profile and slope warnings. Built-in tools include a gravity and weight calculator (kg versus newtons), an interior and density guide, an Earth–Mars comparison, and a Mars clock showing local time and season at landing sites. The app can load real NASA MOLA elevation data, and every modelled value is clearly labelled as modelled. By putting terrain, climate and physics in one place, MARSCOPE makes Mars science easier for students and mission planners to understand and supports early exploration planning.
details:
What it does and how it works
MARSCOPE is a browser-based 3D globe of Mars. You can drag to rotate and scroll to zoom. Three layers (surface imagery, topography and temperature) show the planet in different ways, and each has a legend. Clicking any point opens a panel with its coordinates, elevation, slope, terrain type, gravity, estimated temperature and nearby named features, plus an east–west terrain profile. In route mode you pick a start (A) and destination (B), and MARSCOPE draws a great-circle route and reports its distance, elevation profile, total climb and slope warnings. Extra tabs include a gravity and weight calculator that keeps mass (kg) separate from weight (newtons), an interior and density guide, a surface mineral guide, an Earth–Mars comparison, and a dataset table. A live Mars clock shows local time at Jezero and Gale Craters, plus the season and where the Sun is overhead.

Benefits and intended impact
Mars information is usually scattered across many tools. MARSCOPE puts terrain, climate and physics in one simple interface so students, educators and early mission planners can build intuition about the planet and compare candidate routes. It runs from a single file with no installation.

Honesty about data
Values that are modelled are labelled as modelled on screen, and anything without data shows “Data unavailable”. The route is a candidate over coarse terrain, not a safe-path certification.

Tools and technologies
HTML, CSS and JavaScript with the HTML canvas. There are no external libraries, and the globe is rendered with our own code. We used Claude (Anthropic), an AI assistant, to help write and debug the code. The Mars clock follows the published NASA GISS Mars24 algorithm.

Creativity
We combined a real-time globe, day/night lighting based on actual Mars time, and mission-planning tools in one interface, with a Martian-themed design.

Factors we considered
Scientific honesty (labelling modelled data), readability for non-experts, performance on ordinary laptops, and keeping the scope achievable in 24 hours.
